title: Keep separately feasible controllers from inventing a common source
statement: Given g(0)=0, controllerK1=0/load1/equilibrium1 and K2=1/2/load1/equilibrium2/5 are each feasible under1<=Esecond<=3. A common source would require g(1)=1,g(2/5)=6/5, with secant product-3/25, contradicting monotonicity. Cartesian products of per-controller feasible regions are unsupported.

assumptions: Compatibility is conditional and cannot certify global physical conservativity from finite success. Pairwise or triple-only tests can fail; independently compatible different controllers cannot be multiplied as a common-source portfolio. General noisy acceptance, nonsymmetric feedback, microscopic restrictions and transient dynamics are outside scope. The17-file compiler/results/verifier archive is UNACQUIRED; reported12-cut24-bit replay and six-controller execution are not independently accepted. Original rational coefficient explosion is retained. Established interpolation/conjugacy/cycle ingredients are credited; equally informed retainers can tie. No physical or priority advantage.
costs: Pay original position control/full-vector gradient acquisition, independent curvature/conservativity/calibration warrants, retained history, O(N^3) rational graph operations plus bit costs, optimization/cut selection, later physical feedback and full-cycle resources. Zero later learner calls does not erase acquisition. Absolute energy needs a separately charged energy sensor; checker source access is not learner access.
contract.units: Coordinates are declared nondimensional Euclidean source coordinates; retain calibrated position, full gradient/force, energy and controller units. mu,L,K act in the same force/position units, potential differences in conjugate-energy units. No automatic SI conversion.
contract.obstruction: Acquire current producer code/result certificates before accepting its replay-specific digits, and independently warrant/realize the source and controller interfaces. Retain source-family, uncertain-data and mixed-controller boundaries; mission NOT_ACHIEVED.
